title: Generic radicial-etale factorization of a proper generically finite map
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ and $S$ be nonempty integral separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to S$ be a proper dominant $k$-morphism inducing a finite extension $L=k(X)$ of $K=k(S)$ [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map, def-pc-field-extension]. Then $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and there exists a nonempty dense affine open subscheme $S_0\subseteq S$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum] such that $f_0:X_0=X\times_S S_0\to S_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and has a factorization
$$X_0\xrightarrow{u}T_0\xrightarrow{e}S_0.$$
Here $T_0$ is integral, $u$ is finite and a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism] (a homeomorphism after every scheme base change), and $e$ is finite etale surjective [def-weil-etale-morphism] of constant degree $d\geq1$, meaning $e_*\mathcal O_{T_0}$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-module of constant rank $d$ [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Under the induced function-field inclusions, $k(T_0)$ is the subfield $K_s=\{z\in L:z\text{ is separable over }K\}$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure], and $d=[K_s:K]$. Thus purely inseparable and degree-one extensions are included, and no normality, regularity, or separability of $L/K$ is assumed.

Spreading the purely inseparable part uses Tags 00GQ, 0BR5, 01S2 as in lem-weil-pbc-spread-purely-inseparable-factors. proof.text: The image of $f$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] and dense by dominance, hence equals $S$. Properness gives quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness and finite type by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $S$ Noetherian.

Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $S$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $\eta$ and cover its inverse image by nonempty affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $A\subset K$, $B_i\subset L$ are domains with the indicated fraction fields, compatibly with the generic stalk map [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. Put $C_i=(A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}B_i\subset L$. It is a $K$-linear subspace of the finite-dimensional space $L$, hence finite-dimensional. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] it is a field; since it contains $B_i$ it contains every fraction of $B_i$, so $C_i=L$. The generic fibre of each chart is $\operatorname{Spec}C_i$: maps to this affine fibre are precisely ring maps out of $B_i$ inverting every nonzero element of $A$, by the affine-spectrum and fibre-product universal properties. Its sole point projects to the zero prime of $B_i$, namely the generic point of $X$. Thus the whole set-theoretic fibre over $\eta$ is that one point.

source.place: Tag 02NW (lemma-generically-finite), verification of condition (1); affine localization calculation. Agent argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] using Step 1 and the singleton fibre of Step 2; $S$ has only one irreducible component. Obtain a dense open on which $f$ is finite and choose a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ inside it. Its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $B$ finite over $A$, by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Both are domains with fraction fields $K,L$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Restricting further to $D(a)$ replaces $A,B$ by $A[1/a],B[1/a]$: the affine-spectrum universal property identifies the inverse image with the spectrum of the localized ring. Module generators localize, so finiteness persists.

By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable], $K_s/K$ is separable algebraic and $L/K_s$ purely inseparable. As a $K$-subspace of $L$, $K_s$ has finite dimension. Choose $\alpha$ generating $K_s/K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-primitive-element]. Its monic minimal polynomial $P$ is separable by [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The isomorphism $K[T]/(P)\simeq K_s$ of [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso], together with the power basis of [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], gives $d=\deg P=[K_s:K]\ge1$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localized-separable-polynomial-model] to $A,K,K_s,\alpha$. After inverting a nonzero element of $A$, $P$ descends to a monic $Q\in A[T]$ with $UQ+VQ^{\prime}=1$ for some $U,V\in A[T]$. Also $\alpha\in B[1/a]$ for some nonzero $a\in A$: the same calculation as Step 2 shows $(A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}B=L$, and an element of this localization has a single denominator in $A$. Invert this additional $a$; polynomial identities and module generators remain valid. Set $C=A[T]/(Q)$ and send $T$ to $\alpha\in B$. This embeds $C$ in $B$: by the power basis [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], every element has degree less than $d$; an element evaluating to zero in $L$ has all coefficients zero, since $P$ is the degree-$d$ minimal polynomial and $A\hookrightarrow K$. Thus $C=A[\alpha]$ is a domain, and its fraction field is $K(\alpha)=K_s$.

source.place: Tags 00UB (definition-standard-etale) and 00UC (lemma-standard-etale); denominator and power-basis calculation.

proof.text: The same power basis makes $C$ free of rank $d$ and finite over $A$. In $C$, $VQ^{\prime}=1$, so adjoining the inverse of $Q^{\prime}$ changes nothing. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] to conclude that $e:\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale. It is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over]: $A\to C$ is injective and each element of the finite algebra $C$ is integral. This integrality is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], applied to the finite ring map $A\to C$. The map $C\to B$ is finite: a set generating $B$ as an $A$-module also generates it as a $C$-module. Hence we have $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with composite $f$ on this open.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spread-purely-inseparable-factors] with $A\prime=C$, $E=B$, $K\prime=K_s$. Here $A$ is a Noetherian domain: $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an affine open of the Noetherian scheme $S$ of Step 1, so [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] applies, $C$ is a finite etale domain of fraction field $K_s$, $B$ is finite over $C$ with fraction field $L$, and $L/K_s$ is finite purely inseparable by Step 4. Invert the resulting nonzero $s\in A$. Take $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A[1/s]$, $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}C[1/s]$ and $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/s]$. The lemma gives the universal homeomorphism $u$; the original module generators show it is finite. The localized polynomial $Q$ and its Bezout identity give finite etaleness of $e$ by Step 6 again, and lying over [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over], with integrality from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], gives surjectivity. The localized power basis has $d$ elements, so $e_*\mathcal O_{T_0}$ is free of rank $d$. Localization of a domain at a nonzero element preserves its fraction field, so [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] makes $T_0$ integral with $k(T_0)=K_s$ and the required inclusions. The nonempty open $S_0$ is dense in integral $S$.
